questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design namespace-scoped automation, RBAC, and progressive release patterns using standard CKAD primitives.

## Key Concepts
- ConfigMap-driven orchestration
- kubectl patch in a CronJob
- Rollout status checks and idempotent patches
- Namespace-scoped RBAC (Role/RoleBinding)
- InitContainers for tooling
- Logs via PVC and status stored in ConfigMap
- NetworkPolicy restricting egress to internal canary API

## Code Example
```yaml
# minimal skeleton: CronJob that orchestrates canaries
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: canary-roller
spec:
  schedule: "*/10 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: canary-runner
          containers:
            - name: patcher
              image: bitnami/kubectl:latest
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "echo placeholder"]
          initContainers:
            - name: kubectl-install
              image: bitnami/kubectl:latest
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "kubectl version --client"]
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle partial failures when some Deployments fail to patch?
- How would you ensure the canary_percent value is validated and does not exceed 100?
- What RBAC boundaries would you apply to restrict the CronJob's scope?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical CKAD-level validation workflows that go beyond simple deployments, focusing on per-namespace compliance checks, file-based manifests, and secure external reporting.

## Key Concepts

- Per-namespace Deployments with PVC-mounted manifests
- kubeval and conftest for validation
- ConfigMaps for suites and batch sizing
- Secrets for API credentials
- InitContainer tooling setup
- Sidecar TLS rotation
- Readiness/Liveness probes
- Namespace NetworkPolicy restricting egress

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal skeleton for the per-namespace scanner Deployment
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ns-baseline-scanner
  namespace: placeholder-namespace
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: ns-baseline-scanner
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ns-baseline-scanner
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: install-tools
        image: alpine:3.17
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl jq yq && echo ready"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
      containers:
      - name: scanner
        image: your-registry/ns-baseline-scanner:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: manifests
          mountPath: /manifests
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
      volumes:
      - name: manifests
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: manifests-pvc
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: logs-pvc
      imagePullSecrets:
      - name: reg-creds
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test and verify the validation pipeline in CI/CD?
- What metrics would you collect to monitor this per-namespace scanner?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests secret handling, TLS/mTLS basics, mounting certs, and correct network isolation for a real-world integration.

## Key Concepts
- Secrets and volume mounts
- TLS/Certificates and mTLS basics
- NetworkPolicy egress controls
- Rollout and secret rotation strategies

## Code Example
```javascript
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: tls-secret
type: Opaque
data:
  tls.crt: <base64>
  tls.key: <base64>
  ca.crt: <base64>
```

```javascript
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payments-api
  namespace: prod
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: payments
        image: payments-api:latest
        env:
        - name: TLS_PATH
          value: /certs
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls
          mountPath: /certs
      volumes:
      - name: tls
        secret:
          secretName: tls-secret
```

```javascript
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: payments-egress
  namespace: prod
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: payments-api
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 203.0.113.45/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

> Note: DNS-based egress restrictions are not widely supported in NetworkPolicy; use the processor’s IP in the ipBlock.

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design per-namespace automation for safe, auditable canary rollouts with minimal disruption. It emphasizes idempotence, config-driven behavior, and secure traffic controls.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob scope and schedule
- Namespace-scoped ConfigMaps and Secrets interplay
- InitContainers for tool provisioning
- Patch strategy for container images (kubectl patch, jq)
- Logs via PVC and heartbeat-status tracking
- NetworkPolicy least privilege in a per-namespace context

## Code Example
```javascript
# Minimal CronJob skeleton (yaml shown as JS block per guidelines)
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: canary-roller
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  schedule: "*/5 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: install-tools
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh","-c","apk add --no-cache curl jq kubectl"]
          containers:
          - name: canary-roller
            image: registry.example/canary-roller:latest
            command: ["sh","-c","/scripts/canary-roll.sh"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
          volumes:
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: canary-logs
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you guard against partial failures when some Deployments succeed and others fail during a run?
- What RBAC changes would you add to restrict the CronJob's patch actions to only image fields?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests per-namespace isolation, secret/config usage, InitContainer tooling, PVC-based logs, and network policies in CKAD.

## Key Concepts
- ConfigMap/Secret mounts in Pod
- InitContainer for tooling
- Bash loop with curl and HTTP codes
- PVC-based logging and central ingestion
- Namespace NetworkPolicy scoped to collector

## Code Example
```bash
#!/bin/bash
endpoints=$(cat /etc/metrics/endpoints)	token=$(cat /secrets/metrics-token/token)
while true; do
  for ep in $endpoints; do
    status=$(curl -sI -w '%{http_code}' -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $token" "$ep")
    if [ "$status" != "200" ]; then echo "$ep failed: $status" >> /logs/metrics/summary.log; fi
  done
  sleep 300
done
```

- How would you add idempotent retries and backoff?
- How to test policy changes locally with kind/minikube?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD skills: CronJobs, Jobs, ConfigMaps, Secrets, PVCs, and RBAC in a single cohesive workflow. Emphasizes idempotence, cleanup, and rollback in a real maintenance task.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob and Job lifecycle
- ConfigMap and Secret integration
- PersistentVolumeClaim mounts
- ServiceAccount with RoleBinding
- ttlSecondsAfterFinished and history limits
- Observability: logs and data integrity

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: daily-archive
  namespace: data-archive
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: archive-sa
      ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          volumes:
            - name: data
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: data-pvc
            - name: archive
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: archive-pvc
          containers:
            - name: archiver
              image: myorg/archive-tool:latest
              imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
              envFrom:
                - configMapRef:
                    name: archive-config
                - secretRef:
                    name: archive-creds
              volumeMounts:
                - name: data
                  mountPath: /data
                - name: archive
                  mountPath: /archive
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "archive --older-than ${ARCHIVE_DAYS} --src /data --dst /archive"]
              resources:
                requests:
                  cpu: "100m"
                  memory: "128Mi"
                limits:
                  cpu: "500m"
                  memory: "512Mi"
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 1000
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test idempotency if ARCHIVE_DAYS changes while a run is mid-flight?
- What monitoring would you add to alert on failed archives and ensure timely rollback?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests the ability to implement namespace-scoped policy tooling, performing API reads/patches, triggering rollouts, and handling observability with PVC logs and external reporting.

## Key Concepts

- Kubernetes API: list and patch Deployments in a namespace
- imagePullPolicy Always and rolling updates via annotations
- InitContainer to prepare kubectl
- PVC-backed logs collection
- ConfigMap and Secret for runtime config and webhook credentials
- Readiness/Liveness probes
- Namespace NetworkPolicy for restricted egress

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: image-pull-policy-enforcer
  namespace: <target-namespace>
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: image-pull-policy-enforcer
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: image-pull-policy-enforcer
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: install-kubectl
        image: alpine:3.18
        command: ["sh","-c","apk add --no-cache curl kubectl"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
      containers:
      - name: enforcer
        image: myorg/enforcer:latest
        envFrom:
        - configMapRef:
            name: enforcer-config
        - secretRef:
            name: enforcer-webhook-creds
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: enforcer-logs
      restartPolicy: Always
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test idempotency of patches in CI/CD?
- What are failure modes if the webhook is unreachable?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates CKAD competencies in CronJob scheduling, InitContainers for tooling bootstrap, PVC-mounted database operations, health probes, lifecycle hooks, and rollback strategies.

## Key Concepts
- **CronJob**: Scheduled jobs using cron syntax (0 2 * * * for daily at 02:00)
- **InitContainer**: Bootstrap tool installation (sqlite3) before main container runs
- **SQLite Operations**: DELETE with WHERE clause for date filtering, VACUUM for storage reclamation
- **Probes**: readinessProbe and livenessProbe on /healthz endpoint
- **Lifecycle Hooks**: preStop sleep for graceful shutdown
- **PodDisruptionBudget**: minAvailable: 1 ensures availability during disruptions

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: log-pruner
  namespace: ckad-practices
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        metadata:
          labels:
            app: log-pruner
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          initContainers:
          - name: installer
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache sqlite"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: db
              mountPath: /data
          containers:
          - name: pruner
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh", "-c", "sqlite3 /data/logs.db 'DELETE FROM logs WHERE created_at < date(\"now\", \"-30 days\"); VACUUM;'; curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{\"deleted\":\"$(date)\"}' http://ops-portal:8080/api/v1/prune-summary"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: db
              mountPath: /data
            resources:
              requests:
                memory: "64Mi"
                cpu: "100m"
              limits:
                memory: "128Mi"
                cpu: "500m"
            readinessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /healthz
                port: 8080
              initialDelaySeconds: 5
              periodSeconds: 10
            livenessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /healthz
                port: 8080
              initialDelaySeconds: 15
              periodSeconds: 20
            lifecycle:
              preStop:
                exec:
                  command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 5"]
          volumes:
          - name: db
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: logs-pvc
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: log-pruner-pdb
  namespace: ckad-practices
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: log-pruner
```

## Rollback Strategy
Maintain version-controlled YAML manifests in a Git repository. On failure, execute:
```bash
kubectl apply -f log-pruner.yaml --record
kubectl rollout undo cronjob/log-pruner
```
Alternatively, use a GitOps tool like ArgoCD or Flux for automated rollbacks.

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to coordinate InitContainers, sidecars, and config-driven apps in CKAD. Ensures proper volume mounting, file-based reloading semantics, and safe network posture.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainer: pre-flight yamllint validation of /configs
- Config mounting: PVC-backed /configs shared with main container and sidecar
- Sidecar watcher: detects changes and triggers in-app reload via /reload/trigger
- Readiness/Liveness probes: ensure proper pod health
- Namespace NetworkPolicy: restricts egress to internal services only

## Code Example
```yaml
# minimal skeleton (Deployment)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: config-reloader
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: config-reloader
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: lint-configs
        image: busybox
        command: ["sh", "-c", "yamllint /configs/**/*.yaml || exit 1"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config-volume
          mountPath: /configs
      containers:
      - name: main-app
        image: myapp:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config-volume
          mountPath: /configs
        - name: reload-volume
          mountPath: /reload
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
        env:
        - name: RELOAD_PATH
          value: /reload/trigger
      - name: reload-watcher
        image: alpine:latest
        command: ["sh", "-c", "inotifywait -m /configs -e modify,create -e moved_to | while read; do touch /reload/trigger; done"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config-volume
          mountPath: /configs
        - name: reload-volume
          mountPath: /reload
      volumes:
      - name: config-volume
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: config-pvc
      - name: reload-volume
        emptyDir: {}
```

## Why This Is Asked

```yaml
# Minimal skeleton outline (not full manifests):
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: app-token
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: fetch-token
        image: curl:latest
        command: ["sh", "-c", "curl -sS https://vault.local/token -o /tokens/token.txt"]
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /tokens
          name: token-vol

      - name: app
        image: myapp:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /tokens
          name: token-vol
      volumes:
      - name: token-vol
        emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: batch/v1beta1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: rotate-token
spec:
  schedule: "0 */6 * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: rotator
            image: curl:latest

            volumeMounts:
            - mountPath: /secret
              name: secret-vol
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          volumes:
          - name: secret-vol
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to compose Kubernetes primitives for practical automation: CronJobs, Jobs, ConfigMaps, Secrets, and PVCs, plus robust scheduling and rollback.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob scheduling and jobTemplate usage
- ConfigMap and Secret as environment sources
- PVC mounting in Jobs for persistent backups
- Concurrency policy and job history controls
- Rollback and validation workflows

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: db-backup
  namespace: dataops
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 7
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 7200
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: postgres-backup
            image: postgres:15
            env:
            - name: BACKUP_DIR
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: backup-config
                  key: BACKUP_DIR
            - name: DB_HOST
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: backup-config
                  key: DB_HOST
            - name: DB_USER
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: db-credentials
                  key: DB_USER
            - name: DB_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: db-credentials
                  key: DB_PASSWORD
            command:
            - /bin/bash
            - -c
            - |
              DATE=$(date +%Y%m%d)
              BACKUP_FILE="/backups/${DB_NAME}-${DATE}.sql"
              pg_dump -h $DB_HOST -U $DB_USER -d $DB_NAME > $BACKUP_FILE
            volumeMounts:
            - name: backup-storage
              mountPath: /backups
          volumes:
          - name: backup-storage
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: backup-pvc
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Validation Plan
1. Check CronJob creation: `kubectl get cronjob db-backup -n dataops`
2. Verify schedule: `kubectl describe cronjob db-backup -n dataops`
3. Test manual job: `kubectl create job --from=cronjob/db-backup test-backup -n dataops`
4. Monitor job completion: `kubectl get jobs -n dataops -w`
5. Validate backup files: `kubectl exec -it <pod-name> -n dataops -- ls -la /backups`

## Rollback Plan
1. Delete CronJob: `kubectl delete cronjob db-backup -n dataops`
2. Clean up test jobs: `kubectl delete jobs -l job-name=db-backup -n dataops`
3. Remove backup files if needed: Access PVC and delete specific backup files
4. Recreate with corrected manifest if issues persist

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a one-off reconciliation Job that interacts with external services, ensures idempotent processing via a fingerprint, and properly configures InitContainers, Secrets, and backoff behavior. It also checks handling of PVC-mounted data and rollback planning.


## Key Concepts

- Kubernetes Job with backoff and deadline
- InitContainer for bootstrap tooling
- PVC mounting and data access in a one-off task
- yq for YAML extraction
- Idempotent design via server fingerprint key
- Secret and ConfigMap usage for credentials and endpoints
- Rollback and observability considerations


## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: data-ingest-audit-reconcile
spec:
  backoffLimit: 4
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 900
  template:
    metadata:
      name: data-ingest-audit-reconcile
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: reconciler
        image: your-registry/audit-client:latest
        command: ["sh", "-c", "set -e; /bin/reconcile.sh /data/manifests.yaml"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: manifests
          mountPath: /data
      initContainers:
      - name: installer
        image: alpine:3.18
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl jq && curl -L -o /usr/local/bin/yq https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/v4.9.6/yq_linux_amd64 && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: manifests
          mountPath: /data
      restartPolicy: Never
      volumes:
      - name: manifests
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: data-manifests
      imagePullSecrets:
      - name: regcred
```


## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test idempotency in CI/CD?
- How would you scale this for larger manifest sets without timeouts?
- How would you monitor and rollback on failure?

Tests ability to compose Kubernetes primitives (PVC, ConfigMap, Secret, InitContainer), simple HTTP API, file-based persistence, TLS rotation, and network controls at CKAD level. Encourages thinking about concurrency, idempotence, and failure modes.

- InitContainer bootstrap
- ConfigMap and Secret usage
- TLS cert rotation sidecar

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: blob-store
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: api
        image: example/api:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet: {path: /health, port: 8080}
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /data
      volumes:
      - name: data
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests CKAD-level design and debugging of StatefulSets, bootstrapping, and network policies under real constraints.

## Key Concepts
- StatefulSet with stable identity and PVC
- headless Service and partitioned rolling updates
- InitContainer for bootstrapping
- PodDisruptionBudget and readiness/liveness probes
- Resource quotas and NetworkPolicy bounds

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: cache-svc
  labels:
    app: cache
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  selector:
    app: cache
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: cache
spec:
  serviceName: cache-svc
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cache
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cache
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: seed
        image: busybox
        command: ["sh", "-c", "echo seed > /data/.seed"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /data
      containers:
      - name: cache
        image: redis:7
        ports:
        - containerPort: 6379
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /data
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "512Mi"
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet: {path: "/ready", port: 6379}
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet: {path: "/live", port: 6379}
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: cache-pvc
  volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata:
      name: cache
    spec:
      accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: cache-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cache
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD skills for multi-namespace automation, pod networking, and safe secret handling via Secrets and ConfigMaps.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob in a Namespace; PVC mounts
- InitContainer installation; jq usage
- Secret/ConfigMap usage; status tracking
- NetworkPolicy scoping; per-namespace egress control

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: metrics-watcher
  namespace: <namespace>
spec:
  schedule: "*/5 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          containers:
          - name: collector
            image: registry.example/metrics-collector:latest
            volumeMounts:
            - name: metrics-pvc
              mountPath: /metrics
            - name: logs-pvc
              mountPath: /logs
            env:
            - name: ENDPOINT
              value: "https://metrics-portal:9090/api/v1/digest"
            - name: API_TOKEN
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: metrics-secret
                  key: api-token
          initContainers:
          - name: install-tools
            image: appropriate/curl
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache jq && mkdir -p /logs"]
          volumes:
          - name: metrics-pvc
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: metrics-pvc
          - name: logs-pvc
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: logs-pvc
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8080
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8080
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you rotate the API token without restarting the CronJob?
- What are trade-offs of using a CronJob for real-time metrics vs. a DaemonSet collector?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to wire ConfigMaps, Secrets, and network policy in a simple feature-flag pattern.

## Key Concepts
- ConfigMaps as feature flags; in‑pod live reload without restart
- InitContainers and Secrets for defaults and credentials
- Sidecar for TLS rotation; readiness/liveness probes
- Namespace NetworkPolicy restricting egress

## Code Example
```yaml
# minimal skeleton for Deployment + ConfigMap (simplified)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: flag-service
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: flag-service
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: flag-service
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: flag-server
        image: myorg/flag-server:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        volumeMounts:
        - name: flags
          mountPath: /flags
      initContainers:
      - name: init
        image: alpine:3.18
        command: ["/bin/sh","-c","apk add --no-cache curl jq"]
      volumes:
      - name: flags
        configMap:
          name: feature-flags
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you add a cache invalidation strategy if flags frequently change?
- How would you handle large flag sets and memory constraints?
